data.title: Glencore, Mercuria pursuing Venezuela aluminum smelter deal - Bloomberg
data.description:
Miner Glencore (GLCNF) (GLNCY) and commodities ​trader Mercuria Energy are among firms interested in a ‌potential deal for Venezuela's largest aluminum smelter, Bloomberg reported Friday.

The two companies are each in discussions with the Venezuelan government about ​a deal for the Venalum smelter, and while it is not clear what structure any agreement might involve, talks have included ​operating the facility and gaining access to the aluminum ⁠it produces, according to the report.

Venalum is controlled by the Venezuelan state and was once a major aluminum producer whose output collapsed after years of under-investment, power shortages, and economic turmoil; it has a capacity to produce 430K tons/year of primary aluminum.

Glencore (GLCNF) (GLNCY) had ties to Venezuela's state-owned aluminum sector more than 20 years ago and later provided financing to the country's aluminum producers; it also built an extensive oil-trading relationship with state-owned PDVSA.

data.title: Apollo in talks to acquire J&J’s orthopedics unit - Bloomberg
data.description:
Apollo Global Management (APO) ​is in talks to acquire ‌Johnson & Johnson's (JNJ) DePuy Synthes orthopedics unit in a deal that could value it at close ​to $20B, Bloomberg reported late Friday.

An agreement could be reached within several weeks, although the talks could still end without a deal, another bidder could emerge, or J&J (JNJ) could decide to spin off the business as a publicly traded company, according to the report.

J&J (JNJ) announced plans last October to separate its orthopedics business, which reportedly has attracted interest from several private equity firms.

DePuy Synthes, which makes devices used in hip and knee replacements, generated $9.3B in sales in 2025, and J&J (JNJ) has said it would be the world's largest orthopedics company if it becomes a standalone entity.

data.title: Saudi shuts pipeline that was vital Hormuz bypass as new front opens in Middle East war
data.description:
Saudi Arabia said Friday it has shut the crucial East-West pipeline that had allowed it to continue exporting crude oil after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, saying it was attacked multiple times by drones fired by militias in Iraq.

The East-West pipeline can carry as much as 7M bbl/day of crude a day, 750 miles from Saudi Arabia's oil-producing heartland on the Persian Gulf to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, where the kingdom has been able to ship millions of barrels of oil to customers around the world.

The pipeline attacks come as Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen strengthened their hold on the southern Red Sea's Bab al-Mandeb strait, another key chokepoint for Saudi oil exports, taking control of an island in the strait and a nearby mainland coastal town, capping a series of swift gains in the area that are believed to have been guided by Iran's Revolutionary Guards.

Attacks on the pipeline earlier this year damaged a pumping station and reduced capacity by ~700K bbl/day, and Saudi Aramco (ARMCO) restored the pipeline to its full capacity within days, but the latest attacks reportedly targeted several pumping stations.

Saudi crude oil production has already fallen to the lowest levels in more than three ‌decades, the International ⁠Energy Agency said Friday in the latest oil market report, declining to 6M bbl/day in August from 8.3M bbl/day in July and 9.4M bbl/day on average last year.

The latest developments ​could represent a major escalation in the Middle East war if oil supplies are reduced through a second major corridor that further raises oil prices; Reuters reported Friday that Saudi Arabia has asked the Trump administration for military help.

The Houthi advances and any significant damage to the East-West pipeline could boost oil prices toward $120/bbl, although the extent of the gains will depend on the extent of the damage, according to Hamad Hussain of Capital Economics.

Crude oil futures pulled back Friday in an apparent bout of profit-taking after a string of gains but ended the week sharply higher in reaction to the escalating Middle East conflict.

"Although much of today's price pullback appears attributable to talk of Middle East countries discussing a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and some bearish demand aspects to today's monthly IEA report, the larger negative driver in our opinion is simply a deserved market correction following this week’s dramatic gains," Ritterbusch & Associates said in a note.

On Friday, front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for October delivery dipped 2.4% to $100.05/bbl, front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for November delivery sank 2.8% to $104.61/bbl, and front-month Nymex October natural gas (NG1:COM) slipped 0.1% to $2.831/MMBtu.

For the week, Nymex crude and Brent crude jumped 9.4% and 8.5%, respectively, while Nymex natural gas fell 4.8%.

Oil supply disruptions due to the Iran war, along with Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries, pushed the U.S. national average diesel price this week past $6/gal for the first time.

Front-month Nymex ULSD (HO1:COM) for October delivery jumped 9.2% this week to $4.9593/gal, on Thursday posting its highest settlement value since April 2022, and front-month Nymex RBOB gasoline (XB1:COM) for October delivery gained 2.9% to $3.3072/gal.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), gained 1.7% this week.

data.title: Olema drops after hours on AstraZeneca Etcamah data
data.description:
• Olema Pharmaceuticals (OLMA), which is developing the estrogen receptor antagonist (CERAN) and selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) palazestrant, is down ~15% in after-hours trading Friday after AstraZeneca (AZN) disclosed the failure of its own SERD and CERAN, Etcamah (camizestrant), as a first-line breast cancer treatment.
  • Palazestrant is in phase 3 development in a collaboration with Novartis (NVS) as a first-line treatment in combination with the CDK 4/6 inhibitor Kisqali (ribociclib) for metastatic breast cancer.
  • It is also in phase 3 as a second- and third-line monotherapy.

data.title: AstraZeneca's Etcamah fails in late-stage trial as first-line breast cancer treatment
data.description:
• AstraZeneca's (AZN) recently approved Etcamah (camizestrant) failed in a phase 3 trial as a first-line treatment in combination with Pfizer's (PFE) Ibrance (palbociclib) for HR+, HER2- breast cancer. 
  • Results from the SERENA-4 trial showed that the combination did not improve progression-free survival vs. Ibrance + the aromatase inhibitor Arimidex (anastrozole) with statistical significance. The trial enrolled about 1,400 individuals with no systemic treatment for metastatic disease.
  • Etcamah is also in two other phase 3 trials, CAMBRIA-1 and CAMBRIA-2, that have enrolled about 10,000 patients examining the drug in individuals  with intermediate and high risk of recurrence in the adjuvant setting as monotherapy, in combination with CDK4/6 inhibitors, and following CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment.
  • Etcamah received accelerated approval earlier in September for those with breast cancer who possess an estrogen receptor-1 (ESR1) mutation, which can be discovered during aromatase inhibitor and CDK 4/6 inhibitor therapy.

data.title: U.S. court strikes down DoE emergency order delaying Michigan coal plant retirement
data.description:
The U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit on Friday struck down the U.S. Department of Energy's emergency order that kept a Michigan coal plant running past its planned retirement date, saying the order exceeded federal authority after state regulators had approved the plant's retirement.

The DoE issued an emergency order in May 2025 to keep CMS Energy's (CMS) J.H. Campbell plant operating past its retirement date, saying it was necessary to provide stable energy to the grid, and the department has since reissued the emergency order six times.

A three-judge panel of the D.C. Circuit sided with the environmental groups and the Michigan attorney general that challenged the order, saying there was no real emergency under the law.

Consumers Energy (CMS) has spent $259M so far to maintain the plant's operations beyond the original May 2025 retirement, which opponents of the order have said likely will be paid by families and businesses in the Midwest.

The company said it is reviewing the court ruling but in the meantime will keep the plant operating under terms of the most recent DoE order that extends its directive through mid-November.

data.title: Gold little changed even as U.S. inflation data supports Fed rate-hike bets
data.description:
Gold futures finished little changed Friday as a pullback in oil prices helped offset the impact of a U.S. inflation report that increased expectations for an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve next week.

The Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics reported the Consumer Price Index rose 3.4% in August after rising by the same margin in July, in line with economists' expectations, but increasd 0.4% last ‌month, more than expected ⁠after edging up 0.1% in July.

U.S. gasoline prices gained 3.9% after two straight monthly declines, accounting for more than a third of the CPI increase over the month, while other motor fuels, which include diesel, jumped 9.6% and 44% Y/Y in August.

Gold gained more than 1% in the previous session after the Producer Price Index for final demand rose by a greater-than-expected 0.4% last month and advanced 5.4% in the 12 months through August after rising 4.8% in July.

Traders are now pricing in an 87% chance of a rate hike at ​the Fed's policy meeting next week, up from 67% ​before the ⁠inflation data, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

Still, "while the markets appear to be placing their proverbial bets on a hike, it's likely that members of the FOMC won't be quite as unequivocal," Kyle Rodda from Capital.com said in a note. "The doves on the committee, of which there are many, are likely to argue the case that the dip in annual core inflation justifies patience."

Gold and silver remain within a range of strong support, and if the Fed does raise rates next week, "it's symbolic since the bond market had already tightened," Peter Cardillo of Spartan Capital wrote.

Front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for September delivery gained less than 0.1% on Friday to $4,366.20/oz, and front-month Comex September silver (XAGUSD:CUR) climbed 0.4% to $64.554/oz; for the full week, gold and silver fell 1.4% and 2.6%, respectively.

data.title: Sernova shareholder backs Seraxis takeover proposal
data.description:
• Steven Sangha has entered into a voting and support agreement with Seraxis Holdings to support its proposed acquisition of all securities of Sernova Biotherapeutics (SVA:CA).
  • Under the proposed transaction, each Sernova common share would be exchanged for 0.0112746082 Seraxis common shares.
  • Sernova shares issued from the upcoming private placement would receive a higher exchange ratio of 0.0132400349 Seraxis shares per Sernova share.
  • Sangha has agreed to vote his Sernova securities in favor of the transaction and restrict their disposal while the Voting Agreement remains in effect.
  • Sangha controls 39.7M Sernova shares, 53.6M warrants, convertible debentures worth $2.9M, and 2.54M options, representing about 10.5% ownership on a non-diluted basis and 30.0% on a partially diluted basis.
  • His convertible debentures are currently subject to 9.99% or 19.99% conversion blockers, limiting his ability to convert them into Sernova shares.

data.title: EverCommerce boosts share buyback plan by $25M, lifting total to $325M
data.description:
• EverCommerce (EVCM) said on Friday that its BOD approved a $25M increase to its existing $300M share repurchase program.
  • The increase brings the company's total approved buyback authorization to $325M, valid through December 31, 2027.
  • The company may repurchase shares in the open market at prevailing prices or through negotiated off-market transactions.
  • The program does not require the company to buy any specific amount of shares and can be modified, suspended, or discontinued at the company's discretion.
  • The company expects to fund the repurchases using cash on hand.

data.title: Oracle reveals $700M in additional restructuring costs tied to layoffs
data.description:
Oracle (ORCL) revealed an additional $700M in restructuring costs tied in part to layoffs, according to a Friday filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

"Subsequent to August 31, 2026, our management supplemented the 2026 Restructuring Plan by approximately $700 million to reflect additional actions that we expect to take," the filing reads. "These costs will be recorded to the restructuring and other expense line item within our condensed consolidated statements of operations through the end of the plan. We recorded $167 million and $415 million of restructuring expenses in connection with the 2026 Restructuring Plan for the three months ended August 31, 2026, and 2025, respectively."

The extra $700M increased the "2026 Restructuring Plan" to $2.8B. It will be used for "employee severance costs, contract termination costs and certain other exit costs to improve our cost structure prospectively."

Oracle's workforce has been reduced by about 21,000 year over year as the company pours money into AI infrastructure.
